Source: Otter.ai recording "Rousselot - Whey + Collagen", https://otter.ai/u/2-a4DWLvb-1Z5tHqsJEsHdBFRaM, recorded 9 Nov 2026 11:43, 19m 52s. Speaker labels are Otter's.

[00:10] Speaker unknown: Hello everyone. My name is Staske. I'm a technical sport manager at Russolo, and today I would like to talk to you about something that is impacting many sport nutrition brands. When you think about sports, the key ingredient that comes to mind, the most popular one, is weight. But yeah, the weight price is increasing. Discussed this morning already because the supply is booming, and the supply just can't follow. So that is a bit of a difficulty, and one of the solutions could be replacing part of the weight by collagen and really combining both to have benefits of both. We really see it as a possible solution, a complementary duo, which I would like to call the protein power couple. But before I would like to talk more about the solution, let's first dive a bit more into the market situation. Has been touched upon already by previous presenters, but really, the way demand continues to outpace supply via Z, while way super popular, and only the amount of launches of food supplements, beverage supplements has increased over the years. So really steady growth we see the last two years with an annual growth rate of seven and a half percent.  So because of that, because of this increased demand, really prices are going up as well, so that's been a major topic here. Everyone agrees on this this morning. Prices of whey keep on increasing. So the biggest growth yet was in 24 to 25 with a growth rate of 8.7. So really, when you look at several years, the way is increasing the prices. So might be some fluctuations, as discussed upon earlier. But really, the trend is prices are only going up. Why is that? Why do we see that new launches with the prices of retail are going higher? Because in 2023 the price of a ton of whey protein concentrate of 80% was 5.7 k, whereas in 2026 it's almost 32 k. So really, in just three years' time, it's almost a sixfold, and this is making life for sports nutrition brands difficult. Markets are lower and the formulation costs are getting higher. Do we expect whey prices to stay yes or no like this so high? Actually, a lot of friends used to say like okay or asking when are prices going down, but actually factors driving this market are showing us that those prices will be here to stay. Unfortunately, for the whey, of course. Why is this? Key factors already been touched upon a little bit, but I'm going to explain it a bit more in detail. Supply and demand balance. So, whey super popular in sports nutrition. Demand keeps on growing, and why is that? In the past, it was really about sports nutrition, about the real athletes and the gym goers, etc. And you could find way products more in the gyms and in really like the the shops with sports nutrition. But now it's everywhere. We see it everywhere. We see it in the gas stations, in supermarkets. It's available for everyone because really, it's not only about the sporters anymore, but it's also for the the active lifestyle people. The robot are a bit less sporty, but more average people, let's say. Also, there's a big demand from GLP-1 users, the ones that are on the drugs. They really are, yeah, getting the advice of taking an extra protein because they need to sustain their muscle mass. And a lot of people today are on GLP-1 drug use, and I think that those people, yeah, it will only increase that that amount of people. Also, in new areas like in China, we see a protein trend. So there's also like a high demand in protein. So really, a lot of demand here. And as explained before already, supply can't follow up. Isn't that flexible? Because actually whey is a byproduct for cheese production, and it's not straightforward to increase your production because it is difficult. And like I said before, we really need to look at the future. What can we do? So yeah, that's quite difficult. So also in the in reproduction, the production costs are rising. Gas is costly. Electricity is costly. It's difficult to find the right people to work in this industry.  The job of farmer isn't so attractive anymore. Also, the operational costs, as I explained before, so there's a lot of filtration here. A lot of energy costs, and then you also have, of course, yeah, a bit of uncertainty in the world. You have geopolitical conflicts. You have tariffs one day. Have tariffs. The other way, other day you don't have it anymore. Also, like climate change, this is really impacting the the dairy production as well. So a lot of key drivers that indicate that the whey prices will remain high. So people should no longer ask when will whey prices go down, but what can we do to work around this? So really, how can we adapt? There are three adaptation strategies. One is increase the price of your product, but of course this is not a very popular thing to do. Consumers will not be happy with this. Then you have the shrinkflation, so you offer less at the same price. It's a little bit more, yeah, let's say sneaky, but it's also not something the consumer likes. So instead of offering less or yeah or increasing your price, you could also look at smarter formulations, which I think is the most elegant solutionary and is really an opportunity, because that way you can change the game. You can be more innovative, and you can use protein blends. Blends, sorry, that really change the game and make you stand out and shelf. Also, interesting to know, it was also shown before. It's not a theory anymore. It's happening in real life. So there are more and more launches of products combining whey and collagen, so steady increase over the last couple of years, and yeah, actually an average growth rate of 17.5 percent almost. So it's really something to take into account. This is really something that's happening in the market. For example, this example also shows a combination of 10 grams collagen, 10 grams of whey was already touched upon in the in the past as well. So really, this is a bit explaining the market situation. So replacing part of collagen with whey is interesting for price, but also car supply because the market drivers I've discussed before, like yeah, the the high gas prices, electricity, the the changes in the world, the uncertainty. Of course, collagen also is impacted by that a bit. But collagen is really different in the way the supply chain is is built. It also comes from different sources. So we have the bovine. You can have chicken. You can have fish. You can have porcine. So really, the risk is less spread. And when you look at historical prices, there's not so much fluctuation as a as in way, and it's not going and increasing so dramatically, let's say, as away prices. So we talked a bit about the market situation now. So now let's talk a bit of science. At Truso, we have a premium brand called Pepton, which are collagen peptides for holistic health benefits, and we find it very important that this peptide is built with science. So we do a lot of scientific studies, and part of it, one of the first actions, is sports. So I'd like to explain more in detail here why whey and collagen work better together. So whey and peptone, setting the scene a bit. What is whey? What is pepton? So yes, whey is a complete protein. It's rich in BCAAs, and it's really there for muscle building and muscle repair. That's really the main focus. Peptan is a bit different. It's a hydrolyzed collagen. It is rich in hydroxyproline, which is unique in collagen derived from animal source, and hydroxyproline is really the amino acid that is linked to holistic health benefits. It's also rich in glycine and proline. We also have these amino acids, but really in a very low amount. And glycine and proline are very important for your body for recovery when you have had certain stress conditions. So, for example, when you really sport a lot. So, peptone, we have a lot of science around it, and really shows you that you can move better, you can stay strong, you can recover better. Way is really about muscles, but athletes are not just muscles. You also have when you sport, you have stress on your ligaments, on your tendons, on your joints, and on your bones. And as collagen is the most abundant protein in the human body, it's really important and is really a structural network. And it's yeah a lot. It's a big compound of the extracellular matrix, which really is the movement system, and that supports everything. Everything is kept together, and flexibility and mobility, etc., is being ensured because of that. Therefore, it's really important to take away from the slide. Like these two are no competitors; these two already complementary, and when you add in both, you can have extra additional health benefits. So now I would like to discuss some science that we did where we combined peptan and whey, because of course it's all nice and theory when I say that you can maybe change part of the whey by peptan, but does it really work? What is the impact on performance and recovery? We did a study where we had 22 males, one taking 45 grams of whey, and the other one taking 25 grams of whey and 20 grams of peptone. We assessed performance and recovery, so they had to train for three weeks. In the beginning, they had to do jump hides, and before and after, we took yeah the creatine kinase, which is an enzyme in the blood that marks damage, and we also took it after the training program when again they had to perform jump heights. What did we see there really when we looked at comparing the group that only took weight and the group that took weight and pepton? That results were similar for both recovery and performance. So after the training program, both of them they performed slightly better because, of course, they had a three-week training program, and qua recovery after the first training session. Of course, they had some damage, but it was similar qua way or qua baptan. And also, at the end of the training program, there was no difference between the way group and the way plus baptan group. So actually, the athletes, the recovery was the same, the performance was the same, but you also have more support in your movement system, your musculoskeletal system, and additional health benefits when you add in peptone. Another study we did was peptan because, as I I talked to you before, we had done quite some research on our peptone brand. Is focused on recovery because it's not only important for an athlete to perform during the session, but also to recover fast to be ready for the next session. So here we did a study with let's say 24 males. They had to take in for seven days, pepton or placebo with vitamin C, so 20 gram peptone. So taken every day, and at day zero they had to do 150 jumps to really induce the soreness and the muscle damage. This was taken 40 minutes before and After exercise, and then after two days, again I had to fill in a questionnaire, and there was a follow-up on muscle soreness and recovery. And what was shown here that actually compared to placebo, the one the group taking peptan had 28% less muscle soreness and 13% faster muscle recovery, so they had less pain and you were faster ready for the next session. So really important here as well. And there's another topic that is yeah quite important really in in the sports market and especially for endurance athletes, namely gut comfort. When you have a lot of stress on your body and a lot of endurance athletes like runners, etc., they can have digestive discomfort because they can have increased gut permeability, and that can lead to elevated amethystine levels in the blood. That can cause inflammation, so this is difficult for sporters to do a good performance. Then, when you have gastric discomfort, so what was the protocol here? The first seven days, either 10 grams peptone or placebo was taken. At day seven, they had to take in peptan 45 minutes before an endurance run, really a run of 70 minutes before the run, endotoxins were measured, and after the run, endotoxins were measured as well. So please also take in mind here: 10 grams of peptone was taken 45 minutes before a run, so it's it was okay for the gut. It's not a heavy thing to take. So it's really also a really good thing to to work as a supplement. Let's say it's not heavy on the stomach. So what were the results actually when you compare the placebo or the the peptan when you took in the peptan, it looked like you didn't do any exercise at all because it was the same result as when you didn't do exercise. But when you took in the placebo, you had more endotoxins in your blood. So it's really an indication that taking in peptan could lessen the amount of endotoxins in your blood and could reduce your digestive discomfort, which then would enable athletes to perform better. Then another study we did was on joint discomfort and joint function. So over time, when you get older, of course, there's a bit of a disruption. Yeah, the the the breakdown of the cartilage can be higher than the repair, let's say, and this can cause joint pain and stiffness and less mobility. So here we did a study with women that had mild knee discomfort, and they had to take in for six months, it was a long study that we did. Eight grams fatten a day, and then they had to fill in a questionnaire on how they felt quad pain and also on how their knees functioned. What the results there? We had to monitoring after three months and also a monitoring after six months. That after three months already there was a significant difference for both joint discomfort and joint function. So they really had less pain, and the functionality of the knees was better. They could do more, and after six months, it increased even further. So that's also super important for people that want to keep moving and be flexible. And then we have, of course, another study. So Ursula is actually the first one that did a study on collagen peptides and sleep on how that could impact sleep quality. That's also important because you can't perform well when you didn't sleep well. So sleep is also important for recovery, but also if you had a good night's rest, you'll be able to focus more. And if you have a team sport that you're practicing, then you can really see like, okay, where's my colleague? Okay, let's hit the ball there. I mean, it's it's important to be really focused on the field as well. So there, we had a study where people had taken SIBO or Peptone 15 grams once a day to yeah, let's say a run-in phase, and then at night seven they did a sleep assessment by polysomnography. So really, that's an objective measurement. So people had a lot of sensors on their head, and it was measured how the sleep quality was. And at the morning of the eighth, people also had to fill in a questionnaire. So that's subjective how they thought that they slept, and they also had to do a Stroop test. So really, what results there, both subjectively and objectively, the quality of the sleep of the group taking in peptan increased. So the number of awakenings really reduced from around 30 to 22, something like that, when measured objectively via the sensors, and the people subjectively said like I slept better. I didn't wake up twice, but more one time. So both cases there, they felt like they slept better, and they also had to do a stroop test, which is really something like you see red or green, and then you have two buttons, and you have to press the right color. And the group taking it, patron performed perfectly, 100%. The group that took the placebo performed a bit less. So really, there the reactivity was also a bit less there. So this is also important to take away. Sports nutrition is not only focusing on performance, but also recovery, also sleep quality, also good health, overall well-being and comfort, and that you can boost with with collagen peptides. So, really, to wrap up things, whey and peptan they're better together. There's no competition, but they should be really combined together to have all the benefits possible for athletes or even for active lifestyle people. A muscle building, muscle repair, recovery. That's that's the main focus. But pap tan can deliver so much more and can really make your brand stand out of the shelf. It is something that is so abundant in our body, the collagen, and it will help with the whole movement system to support everything. So your muscles will also work better. You can't just have better and stronger muscles. You need to have everything stronger and more flexible, and working together, and Pathan can do that for you. Additionally, also holistic health benefits, so you move better, you recover faster, and you stay stronger. So that was it for my part. Really, for the application advantages, we talked about why it's interesting to combine both proteins for prices. prices due to the market situation. We also talked about scientifically why it's important because you can have additional health benefits, but also there are a lot of application advantages, and therefore I would like to invite you to the roundtable sessions where you can really discuss more in detail and show you examples and really help you with incorporating collagen

summary.Summary: Tess Plaquet (technical sport manager, Rousselot) argued that whey prices are here to stay and that the elegant answer is "smarter formulations": replacing part of the whey with collagen peptides rather than raising prices or shrinking packs [00:10]. Her market evidence was whey product launches growing seven and a half percent a year over the last two years, the biggest price growth in 24 to 25 at 8.7, and a tonne of WPC80 going from 5.7k in 2023 to almost 32k in 2026, almost sixfold, with drivers (GLP-1 users, China, active lifestyle consumers, whey being a cheese byproduct, energy, labour, tariffs and climate) that she said will keep prices high [00:10]. Launches combining whey and collagen are growing at almost 17.5 percent a year, often at 10 g plus 10 g, and collagen's supply is spread across bovine, porcine, chicken and fish with far less price volatility [00:10]. Her science was Rousselot's Peptan studies: 22 men on 45 g whey or 25 g whey plus 20 g Peptan for three weeks showed similar recovery and performance; 20 g Peptan with vitamin C for seven days gave 28% less muscle soreness and 13% faster recovery than placebo; 10 g before a 70-minute run held blood endotoxins at the no-exercise level; 8 g a day improved knee discomfort and function in women at three and six months; 15 g a day cut night awakenings from around 30 to 22 and the Peptan group scored 100% on a Stroop test [00:10]. The recording ends mid-sentence as she invites the room to the roundtables.
summary.Key takeaways:
- Whey launches (supplements and beverages) have grown steadily for two years at seven and a half percent a year; the biggest price rise was in 24 to 25 at a growth rate of 8.7 [00:10].
- A tonne of 80% whey protein concentrate was 5.7k in 2023 and is almost 32k in 2026, almost sixfold in three years [00:10].
- She said the drivers mean "those prices will be here to stay": demand from active lifestyle consumers, GLP-1 users advised to take extra protein, and China; whey is a byproduct of cheese and cannot be scaled easily; gas, electricity, labour, filtration costs, tariffs, geopolitics and climate all push the same way [00:10].
- Three brand responses: raise the price, shrinkflation, or smarter formulation with protein blends, which she called the most elegant and an opportunity to stand out on shelf [00:10].
- Launches combining whey and collagen are growing at almost 17.5 percent a year; a 10 g collagen plus 10 g whey product was the example [00:10].
- Collagen's supply is spread across bovine, porcine, chicken and fish and its historical prices show far less fluctuation than whey [00:10].
- Whey is a complete protein rich in BCAAs for muscle building and repair; Peptan is hydrolysed collagen rich in hydroxyproline, glycine and proline, pitched at ligaments, tendons, joints and bone; "these two are no competitors" [00:10].
- 22 men, 45 g whey against 25 g whey plus 20 g Peptan, three weeks of training, jump height and creatine kinase: recovery and performance were similar in both groups [00:10].
- 24 men, 20 g Peptan with vitamin C or placebo for seven days, then 150 jumps: 28% less muscle soreness and 13% faster muscle recovery than placebo [00:10].
- 10 g Peptan for seven days then 45 minutes before a 70-minute run: endotoxins were the same as without exercise, while placebo rose; she said this "could lessen" endotoxins and "could reduce" digestive discomfort [00:10].
- Women with mild knee discomfort, 8 g a day for six months: significant improvement in discomfort and function at three months, further at six [00:10].
- Sleep: 15 g a day, polysomnography on night seven: awakenings fell from around 30 to 22, subjective sleep improved, and the Peptan group scored 100% on a Stroop test against a weaker placebo group [00:10].
- Rousselot offers roundtables on application advantages and help incorporating collagen [00:10].
summary.For Vita Actives: Rousselot is selling the same brand problem we sell into (whey cost and supply) with a different answer: partial replacement of whey with collagen, backed by a head-to-head showing no loss of recovery or performance at 25 g whey plus 20 g Peptan [00:10]. My reading is that IsoClr: Pea competes for the same "smarter formulation" slot in a brand's whey review, and the pitch should match hers in form: a cost and supply argument first, then evidence that a blend performs. We do not have a head-to-head of this kind for pea; that is the gap (my reading). Her collagen supply story (four animal sources, little volatility) is the kind of supply-security argument a plant protein can make more strongly (my reading). Whey plus collagen clear drinks were named by Nick Morgan earlier; a clear pea plus collagen format is a possible combination rather than a competition (my reading). The health claims here are Rousselot's own studies, with her hedges; none are ours. Relevance high: protein blends and whey pricing.

Otter.ai's automatic summary, as received. Not ours.

Nick Morgan discusses the evolving consumer landscape, communication strategies, and product formats within the longevity and healthy aging market.

## Market Communication
**Nick** notes that while "longevity" is a technical term, consumers connect more with concepts like "energy," "vitality," and "cellular health." Most brands avoid technical "hallmarks of aging" in lead copy, as only 4% to 9% of products utilize them effectively for a general audience.
**Consumer Trends**
*   Longevity is increasingly linked to women's health (menopause) and sports nutrition.
*   "Cellular health" has become a widely used surrogate for longevity.

## Product Strategy
**Nick** emphasizes that success in 2026 requires selling routines rather than single products. Brands should focus on multifaceted approaches that integrate into daily habits and rituals.
**Pricing and Ingredients**
*   Common ingredients include **resveratrol**, **CoQ10**, **ubiquinol**, and **spermidine**.
*   Longevity products command premium pricing; for example, even traditional ingredients like **creatine** can be repositioned as high-end longevity products through better storytelling.
*   The brand **Solero** is cited as an example of a successful routine-based model using AM, PM, and monthly "reset" products.

## Future Formats
The longevity category is moving beyond the standard capsule format, which currently accounts for 70% of the market. New delivery methods are increasing accessibility and consumer engagement.
**Emerging Delivery Methods**
*   Liquids, gummies, chocolates, and energy drinks (e.g., drinks containing **NAD**).
*   Precision delivery methods such as injection pens/cartridges.
*   Integration into broader categories like hydration and sports nutrition, exemplified by the brand **Centenarian**.

summary.Summary: Miguel (business development) and Brian Keogh (chief scientific officer) of Nuritas, Dublin, presented the company's own AI platform for finding bioactive peptides and the evidence for PeptiStrong, a fava bean protein hydrolysate. The AI takes a mechanism of action or a consumer need and returns candidate peptides for in vitro and in vivo work, about two years from first hypothesis to result [00:20]. PeptiStrong is said to target the mTOR pathway to build muscle and the NF kappa B pathway to lower inflammation; in a murine hind-limb unloading model it prevented 50% of the muscle loss [03:56]. Three human trials were shown: an immobilisation study in the Netherlands against a milk protein concentrate control, where strength came back to baseline and muscle protein synthesis was higher; a 14-day study in a Dublin sports clinic where strength went above baseline within two and a half weeks of a damaging exercise bout; and a KGK trial in Canada in untrained men and women, with faster strength gains at day 28 and 56, lower GDF15 and more bone mineral content [03:56]. Nuritas says PeptiStrong boosts protein rather than competing with it, and could add to creatine, leucine and HMB [03:56]. Claims rest on EFSA protein claims; Vivatis is the partner in Central and Eastern Europe, Nuritas has been active in Poland for six months, and it is developing a product with Tantus [13:50].
summary.Key takeaways:
- Nuritas's proprietary AI goes from a mechanism or consumer need to peptide candidates, then in vitro and in vivo, in about two years on average [00:20].
- PeptiStrong is a protein hydrolysate from fava bean; the speaker says its peptides target mTOR (muscle building) and NF kappa B (inflammation) [03:56].
- Keeping muscles healthy was linked to a 17% decrease in all-cause mortality [03:56].
- Murine hind-limb unloading: PeptiStrong prevented 50% of the muscle loss [03:56].
- Immobilisation trial (Netherlands, males only): the control was milk protein concentrate, not a placebo; muscle lost and regained was the same, but strength came all the way back to baseline and FSR was higher with PeptiStrong [03:56].
- Damage trial (Dublin sports clinic, 14 days' supplementation, isokinetic dynamometer): strength above baseline within two and a half weeks; irisin rose then returned to normal, myostatin was tracked [03:56].
- KGK trial (Canada, untrained men and women, DEXA, supervised training): stronger quicker at day 28, kept at day 56; GDF15 fell with training load; bone mineral content rose, "a kind of a serendipitous finding" [03:56].
- Nuritas positions PeptiStrong as a booster of protein and a partner for creatine, leucine and HMB: "we're not competing with protein" [03:56].
- Claims on pack rest on EFSA protein claims; the regulatory manager has been "creatively defining" others [13:50].
- A library of more than 9 million peptides; next is a non-hormonal sleep peptide, formulated by Vivatis for CEE; six months active in Poland; a development project with Tantus [13:50].
summary.For Vita Actives: PeptiStrong is sold into our customers' muscle, recovery and healthy-ageing products as an add-on to protein and creatine, not a replacement; Nuritas said so explicitly [03:56]. My reading: that makes it a stacking partner for CreaWin and IsoClr: Pea in a recovery formula rather than a competitor, and a plant peptide beside a clear pea protein isolate is a coherent vegan story. The trial design matters when a customer quotes it: the Netherlands control was milk protein concentrate, so the headline strength result is against a dairy protein, not a placebo [03:56]. The commercial map matters too: Vivatis distributes in CEE, Nuritas has been in Poland six months and is developing a product with Tantus, which shows which Polish makers are formulating active-nutrition ingredients [13:50]. **Nuritas** presented their AI-driven approach to discovering bioactive plant-based peptides, specifically focusing on the performance and longevity benefits of **PeptiStrong**.

## Discovery Technology
**Miguel** introduced **Nuritas** as an R&D-focused company based in Dublin that utilizes a proprietary artificial intelligence platform to identify new peptide molecules. The process involves defining a mechanism of action or consumer need and using the **AI** to narrow down candidates for subsequent *in vitro* and *in vivo* testing. This method aims to reduce the discovery timeline to approximately two years while increasing cost-efficiency and accuracy. **Miguel** also noted that the company maintains a library of over 9 million peptides, including a new non-hormonal peptide for sleep.

## PeptiStrong Research
**Brian** detailed the functionality of **PeptiStrong**, a protein hydrolysate derived from fava bean, which acts by activating or inhibiting specific biological pathways. 
*   **Biological Mechanisms**: The product targets the **mTOR** pathway for muscle building and the **NF kappa B** pathway to reduce inflammation. 
*   **Clinical Evidence**: 
    *   An immobilization study in the Netherlands showed that **PeptiStrong** helped restore strength to baseline levels compared to milk protein controls during periods of inactivity.
    *   A trial in Dublin demonstrated rapid recovery from muscle damage (DOMS) and elevated beneficial markers like irisin while managing myostatin.
    *   A trial conducted with **KGK** in Canada involving untrained individuals showed that users gained strength faster than a placebo group and exhibited increased bone mineral content.
*   **Synergy**: The peptides are designed to be synergistic with existing supplements like creatine, leucine, or HMB rather than competing with dietary protein.

## Market Strategy
**Miguel** addressed regulatory considerations regarding EFSA claims and mentioned that they work with partners like **Vivatis** to define labelable benefits for customers. He highlighted recent expansion into Poland and emphasized their openness to new partnerships through the **Remedy CDMO** platform, noting a current development project with **Tantus**.

Oliver introduces Kaneka Ubiquinol as a superior, bioactive form of Coenzyme Q10 for cellular energy and health.

## Product Overview
**Ubiquinol** is the active, reduced form of **Coenzyme Q10**, which provides direct benefits to the body without requiring conversion by the enzyme diaphorase—an enzyme that decreases with age. 
* **Biological functions**: Acts as a cofactor for cellular energy, an antioxidant, and supports mitochondrial biogenesis.
* **Key benefits**: Supports heart, immune, reproductive, and cognitive health, as well as healthy aging and menopause.
* **Bioavailability comparison**: Blood tests show that 90 mg of **Ubiquinol** provides an equivalent blood level to 300 mg of **Coenzyme Q10**. High doses of **Coenzyme Q10** (above 300 mg) are often ineffective due to limited conversion capacity.

## Manufacturing and Distribution
**Kaneka** produces **Ubiquinol** in Japan and maintains high quality standards through extensive research and various certifications.
* **Formulations**: Available in pure form for soft capsules, gel pills, or gummies, and in a microencapsulated form for diverse dosage formats.
* **Quality assurance**: Supported by over 100 clinical studies, **Halal** certification, and multiple innovation awards.
* **Logistics**: **Kaneka** serves the European market via a warehouse in Belgium to ensure short lead times.

This meeting covers presentations on **NovoSol** technology and the nutritional benefits of **OptiMSM**.

## Technology Overview
**Toshton Sack** presented the **NovoSol** micellar encapsulation technology, which addresses the challenge of limited solubility in lipophilic ingredients.
* **NovoSol** uses a biomimetic delivery system to create a water-soluble, homogeneous liquid concentrate that protects ingredients from stomach acid.
* The process is physical rather than chemical, meaning the identity of the active ingredient remains unchanged.
* Key products include **NovoSol Curcumin**, **NovoSol Astaxanthin**, and **NovoSol Coenzyme Q10**.
* Applications include capsules, liquid shots, and "cap and cap" systems like the **Nourreflex PD** by **Favea**, which separates ingredients to reduce interaction risks.

**Lena Leda** discussed the research regarding **OptiMSM** (methylsulfonylmethane) and its role in human nutrition.
* **OptiMSM** is a sulfur-based nutrient composed of 34% sulfur by weight, oxygen, and two methyl groups.
* The molecule serves structural roles by supporting the synthesis of critical molecules such as glutathione (an antioxidant), keratin, and cartilage.
* Clinical benefits identified include support for joint health, skin health, and exercise recovery.
* **Balcom** manages a broad portfolio including chelated minerals, choline, vitamin K2, and methylfolate.

Ralph introduces **Rhosera**, a cultivated **Rhodiola rosea** ingredient designed to combat anabolic resistance and muscle aging.

## Product Overview
**Ralph** presents **Rhosera**, a botanical ingredient derived from a proprietary cultivation of **Rhodiola rosea**. The product aims to address the health gap caused by an aging population, specifically targeting "anabolic resistance," where aging muscle cells become less efficient at utilizing protein. 

**Cultivation and Quality**
*   **Martin Bauer** utilizes a controlled, integrated cultivation process developed over 10 years to identify three elite mother lines.
*   Unlike wild-harvested plants, which are endangered and prone to adulteration, this cultivated material is grown in Central Europe without pesticides.
*   The cultivated material shows significantly higher concentrations (4 to 5-fold) of key metabolites like **rhodiolene**, **glycosyl**, and **rhodiocyanide A** compared to wild variants.
*   Preclinical data indicates the ingredient upregulates specific genes, including **Pax7** (to activate stem cells) and **myod** (for differentiation), while triggering polyamine pathways.

## Clinical Results
**Ralph** shared findings from a double-blind, placebo-controlled study involving 140 untrained adults aged 55 to 75. Participants received a daily dose of 400mg of **Rhosera** alongside defined training and protein intake.

**Key Outcomes**
*   **Muscle Soreness:** Delayed onset of muscle soreness was reduced by 46% in men and 52% in women.
*   **Physical Performance:** Statistically significant improvements were recorded in chair stand tests, single leg balance, bench press, and leg press.
*   **Longevity Biomarkers:** Improvements were noted in hand grip strength, a critical biomarker for longevity.
*   **Mental Well-being:** Participants reported reduced fatigue, improved quality of life, and increased motivation/social engagement.

## Formulation Guidance
For manufacturers looking to incorporate **Rhosera**, **Ralph** provided several technical recommendations and compliance notes.

**Usage Details**
*   Recommended dosage: 250mg to 350mg per formula.
*   Compatible formats: Tablets, capsules, bars, and V caps.
*   Beverage application: While possible, it is challenging due to the inherent bitterness of **Rhodiola**.
*   Regulatory status: The product is 100% plant-based and sustainable; however, since direct **EFSA** claims for **Rhodiola** are limited, formulators may need to use permitted auxiliary claims related to magnesium or vitamin B to address fatigue.

Thomas presented Solabia Nutrition's approach to successful product launches by addressing the practical limitations of standard industry briefs.

## Marketing Strategy
**Thomas** emphasized that a product must be memorable to succeed in the market. He shared two case studies regarding rebranding:
* **Microbiomex**, a flavonol with prebiotic effects, was rebranded as **Copilot Freedom Probiotic** because "flavorbiotic" was too difficult for consumers to understand and remember.
* **Aronia berry extract**, clinically studied for cognitive benefits, was renamed **Brainberry**, which has become the second largest and fastest-growing product in their portfolio.

## Manufacturing Challenges
Successful products require balancing complex ingredient lists with physical stability and delivery formats. 
* Creating products with high doses of multiple ingredients (e.g., 3–5g of creatine or 5–10g of collagen) can lead to issues with solubility and stomach mixing.
* **Thomas** highlighted a partnership with the CDMO **Tantus** to solve creatine degradation in gummies caused by heat application. By using a cold-pressed tablet method combined with **WhatsApp** (a citrus extract), they maintain the integrity of the creatine while supporting nitric oxide production and blood flow.

## Scientific Validity
To avoid meaningless "science-backed" claims, **Thomas** argued that brands must focus on transparent, rigorous data including dose, population, and placebo-controlled endpoints. 
* **Solabia Nutrition** provides open-source access to their study summaries via their website. 
* An example provided was **Bun Olive**, an olive leaf extract used for skin health and menopause symptoms; all relevant studies were conducted on women by female-led research teams to ensure demographic accuracy.

4. Market implementation through manufacturing and concept demonstration.

**Creatine Innovation**
The specific formulation includes:
* 3 grams of creatine.
* 400 mg of a hesperidin-based ingredient.

The goal of this concept is to maintain physical function through an easy-to-use "chew it, don't shake it" format that fits into a daily routine more effectively than standard supplements.

# The Protein Brewery: Fermotein, a fermented mycelium protein for active and all-in-one nutrition: transcript
Source: Otter.ai recording "Thijs - Fermotein - Remedy CDMO", https://otter.ai/u/ZXyx5ZOSuM5zfKku6YMQxaU1pFA, recorded 22 Oct 2026 15:33, 8m 25s. Speaker labels are Otter's.

[00:00] Speaker 1: Thank you. Let's see. Yeah, my name is Tais Bos. I'm the CEO of the Protein Brewery. I actually have quite a long background in selling and developing protein ingredients. So I was at Fonterra, where I headed up their European whey business, and then at at Cosun selling fava proteins. But now I'm really in a space which I really like, which is selling more complex and more sustainable ingredients. So, yeah, our company is the Protein Brewery. We are a brewery of of proteins, so we are a biomass fermentation company. We grow mycelium in bioreactors and we turn that in a super exciting ingredient. I'm going to tell you a little bit about our company. We're probably one of the youngest companies here, so we exist now for six years. Founded in 2020 from the lab into the pilot plant into a commercial scale facility, what we have now in Breda, in the Netherlands, two 85,000 liter fermenters and expanding rapidly. And we are the first mycelium protein company that has EFSA approval. So since the summer of this year, we can finally sell in Europe, but over the last couple of years, we have developed mainly the market in the U.S. which is why I'm going to give you a few examples of the U.S. market. I hope this works. So this is a little video. Let's see. It should start like this. It's made by one of our operators. It's a bit of an artist impression. So this is our factory of our manufacturing process. You see a lot of oxygen, and you see the mycelium growing in the in the bioreactor. What we make is what we grow is a fungal strain, so it comes from fungi. So we brew that in the bioreactor. It forms these hy-Vee, and it consists of protein, prebiotic fiber, and bioactives. And then ultimately, we take the liquid out of the bioreactor and we turn it into a powder through downstream processing. And that powder is then applied in shakes and applications, like you see here. So it's one of our process operators putting AI video making to the to practice, which is really cool to see. So you heard, I think Nick talking about spermidine around longevity. I think a couple of others, including Tentis, were talking about muscle health. Yeah, we have protein in our ingredient, 50% complete protein, 30% prebiotic fiber. It's mainly chitin and chitosan, which is very specific to our type of fungi. Then it's very rich in spermidine, seven times higher than, for example, in beet germ. So it's about 1700 milligrams per kilo, and then very rich in different types of vitamins, especially choline, precursor for b4. So we have all of these different components into one one ingredient, which we mainly use into active nutrition applications. So yeah, I think this is why I really like selling this ingredient. So it's very new, very novel, but I don't think anything else is is out there on the market that combines combines these type of ingredients into one. As I mentioned, so we have been commercializing this in the U.S. because it took a while, took five years to get approved by FSA in Europe, which we now finally have, but now yeah, we we sell into the U.S. and it's mainly into the all-in-one nutrition segment, which hasn't really evolved yet. I think in in Europe you have the wholemeal replacers like U-well and Wyfoot, but in in the U.S. you have brands like Cajava that have developed a category of their own, and it's basically yeah all the nutrition you need from one one type of powder. It's still small, but it's growing really fast. And everybody knows, of course, the protein powder segment, and then also the the meal replacement segment. And it's literally sitting sitting in between. Yeah, one one example is indeed Iskachava. They're one of the fastest growing brands listed in in retail like Walmart, but also selling a lot through the online stores, and they position themselves really as a protein and fiber combination, which you can use in your everyday ritual. So you, for example, use it in a breakfast smoothie or or over lunch. They like it's still still a small company, but they are super profitable, and actually you can see like different types of formats that they use, like all the way from like two-pound bags, like your standard 1 kg bag of protein powder, to larger tubs, but also single serve bags. And obviously, the price increase increases by the small base that you sell sell into the format. Yeah, a couple of couple of other examples. So, for example, one superfood. I think a lot of you, all of you, will probably know AG1, so like the superfood powders. In the US, now new formats and categories are emerging, also catering into all-in-one nutrition. So you have the superfood, and you combine it with protein and fiber. Obviously, for ingredients such as ours, it's a really good fit because we can add promoting our ingredient to to the superfood category, and then yeah, what we've seen in Europe is like I think it it will come, and and hopefully a couple of CMOs or CDMOs here will will embrace the concept. Meal replacement, so like a meal in a bottle or into a into a powder into a bar has been around for quite a long time. So you all recently sold to Danone, Why Food sold to Nestle. So the big FMCG companies are definitely looking into this. But it's still like a meal replacement concept and not an all-in-one nutrition concept. Then a little bit about promoting in our science. So we see ourselves. Although we're a young company, we invest quite heavily in preclinical and clinical science. So we've done studies on the prebiotic effects of our ingredients, so mainly short-chain fatty acids, microbial and alpha diversity in the gut. Given that our fibers are very different from other fibers that are around in the diet, it has a very positive effect. It has a positive effect on GLP-1, and we did a very interesting study with Nema Live on C. elegans, so the nematodes, where fermentin is proven to increase lifespan in the nematodes by 22% We're doing now a follow-up study on that to get to see what actually causes that that specific result, and we're also going to do a human clinical study on that. So click through this quite quickly on the biological aging clock. So we're doing that together with the University of Wageningen in quarter one, large-scale human clinical trial to yeah to measure that. Yeah, that's it. There it is. Together with with Paul Gössfaifers. Yeah. Then at the moment, so we're we're scaling up our company. We're heavily investing in extra production capacity because being a startup, like we have to, and that's partly my job as a CEO as well. We have to raise money because we're definitely not yet profitable. We're scaling up scaling up the production in our factory in Breidan, and then we're also like commercializing the ingredient in in the U.S. and in Europe. So at the moment we have 10 million servings sold in 2026. Three customers now in the U.S. that have launched with with the ingredient, mainly in the active nutrition space, but also in all-in-one nutrition. A lot of prospects in the European pipeline. So like if you want to try the product, I have it at our table in in the hallway. We have a neutral flavored one and an iced coffee flavor. We've raised quite a bit of money up until now. So, over the last six years, we did three investment rounds. So, we raised 70 million. Nova Holdings, so the the parent company of Nova Nessus and Nova Nordisk is our biggest shareholder, and as I mentioned, we're now now approved by EFSA. We're also approved in Singapore, and we're going after approval in in Australia and in Canada. Then let's see, yeah, where I took this opportunity where we're nominated for one of the top companies to watch by Protein Technology magazine. So if you want to vote for us, that's much appreciated. And if you want to connect with us through LinkedIn, yeah, let us know. And yeah, happy to meet a lot of you and answer your questions in in the breaks in today and tomorrow. Thank you. Thank you very much indeed, Tice.

**Thijs** presents **The Protein Brewery**, a biomass fermentation company specializing in mycelium-based protein ingredients.

## Company Overview
**Thijs** describes **The Protein Brewery** as a six-year-old company founded in 2020 that utilizes bioreactors to grow fungal strains.
*   **Production Infrastructure**: The facility in Breda, Netherlands, currently operates two 85,000-liter fermenters with plans for rapid expansion.
*   **Regulatory Status**: The company has secured **EFSA** approval for sale in Europe as of summer 2024, alongside approval in Singapore. Applications are pending in Australia and Canada.
*   **Financials**: The company has raised 70 million through three investment rounds, with **Novo Holdings** (parent of **Novo Nordisk**) as the largest shareholder.

## Product Details
The core product is a mycelium-based powder derived from fungal hyphae via downstream processing.
*   **Nutritional Profile**: The ingredient consists of 50% complete protein, 30% prebiotic fiber (primarily chitin and chitosan), and is rich in spermidine (1700 mg/kg, seven times higher than wheat germ), vitamins, and choline.
*   **Market Strategy**: While primarily targeting the U.S. "all-in-one nutrition" segment—citing brands like **Ka'Chava** as successful examples—the company is now expanding into Europe following **EFSA** clearance.
*   **Commercial Traction**: As of 2026 projections, the company aims for 10 million servings sold, currently maintaining three customers in the U.S. active nutrition space and a growing European pipeline.

## Scientific Research
**Thijs** emphasizes heavy investment in preclinical and clinical studies to validate the ingredient's health benefits.
*   **Gut Health**: Studies have focused on prebiotic effects, specifically short-chain fatty acids, microbial diversity, and positive effects on GLP-1.
*   **Longevity**: Research using *C. elegans* showed that **Fermotein** increased lifespan by 22%.
*   **Future Studies**: A large-scale human clinical trial regarding biological aging clocks is scheduled for Q1 in collaboration with the **University of Wageningen**.

What specific results will the follow-up study on longevity reveal?

- Speaker 0 - : Complete the follow-up study on C. elegans to determine what causes the observed 22% lifespan increase.
- Speaker 0 - : Conduct the large-scale human clinical study with Wageningen University in Q1 to measure effects using a biological aging clock.

# Holland & Barrett: how longevity science translates into consumer outcomes: transcript
Source: Otter.ai recording "Alex Glover - H&B - Remedy CDMO", https://otter.ai/u/LXa2bHODxRY5s8up7grRiBmKTgI, recorded 22 Oct 2026 15:50, 10m 43s. Speaker labels are Otter's.

[00:00] Speaker 1: Factoring and all the decisions that go with it, and then finally the customer's first question is: Is it on offer? Our next session considers how long Gavity Science translates into the relevant consumer outcomes. From strategic partner Holland and Barrett, please welcome Alex Glover. Probably best use one of those that's up there, I think.
[00:25] Speaker 2: Thank you. Yes, great. Everybody can hear me. So, hello, everyone. My name is Alex. So, I lead the product formulation team at Holden Barrack Global. I'm responsible for all of the own label products that Holden Barrett formulate and develop across the globe. And I'm really happy that you started out there saying is we are with you saying about deciding what to buy because that's really the information that we get as a retailer all the time, is why a customer is choosing to buy our products and it's how we communicate that the border of being scientifically led, a clinical outcome, and combining it with a customer outcome because customers don't speak clinical language, so that's the agenda, which we will skip over. So, there's a photograph of a tortoise on the screen, and I really like this this analogy because it was one of the first lectures I ever had doing my master's program. Was this exact image put up on the screen? So, why is there a tortoise on the screen? This is why there's a tortoise on the screen? A tortoise's biology fundamentally challenges the way we look at aging. A tortoise will live the majority of its life without any disability or ailment. As you compare to a human, we live approximately between 10 and 12 years with either a disability or poor health. So a tortoise fundamentally will challenge the notion that biology is we are destined to age in a poor way. I'm not saying we're all going to live to 200 years, but actually there is a biological plausibility that we can all age better. So it's not just smoke and mirrors. Lifespan to health. Nick touched on this very nicely in his talk about the difference between the two, and it's a really important distinction because I think the category should almost be renamed, not just longevity, because actually, we're not in the business of making people live longer; we're making them live better. How do we do that from a product perspective? So, we're in a very, very fortunate position where we have data of millions of consumers across the globe, and we can see what they're buying and how frequently they're buying it, which is obviously the most important thing that we all, as brand owners, want. Is we want customers not just to buy the product once, we want them to keep buying the product. So, I see a lot of this in the kind of cellular health space and the more novels products in the in the longevity spaces. They promise a lot from mechanism. It's all about sirtuins and parts and telomere lengths, and I think I was on a really interesting panel last week in London with our with our own customers. So we were talking to all of our customers. We had customers from all of our key groups, and we had customers from each of our key markets. And something that really stood out to me was the way that customers talk to us about our products. So we think we can communicate to the customer with the science and the claims, but the way customers talk to us. For example, there was there was a lady in one of our customer groups called Stay Healthies. These are customers around the 50 age group, and she was just saying, "Well, actually, all I want to be able to do is play with my grandchildren, get up out of my chair without making a noise, go on that hike, travel without being uncomfortable, and this is not something that we've seen in clinical literature about how can how can I play with my grandchildren, but actually it's how we translate scientific evidence to help consumers with their problems, and not just looking at what the science is saying. And this really does retain customers. So we see the biggest sales that in our own label portfolio is products that have a clear communicated benefit to joint function, joint comfort, brain function, etc. These things like this, not just focusing on disseminating the clinical literature. So yeah, they do not buy. So this is a really interesting point, and I had a bit of a debate with our science team about this one last week. Customers are not buying into the mechanism. They are buying your product based off how they feel and how they continue to feel taking your product. So, common questions that we get as a retailer all the time is when timescale. When am I going to feel a benefit? What kind of benefit am I going to feel taking the product? And that's when we look to lean on the science because we can say, well, the population we saw a benefit within four weeks, within eight weeks, within six weeks, and with a strong scientific communication strategy that we have as a brand, we can sometimes communicate those things to the customer on pack. Can I measure it? Do I feel an improvement? Can I walk without pain? Can I play longer with my grandchild? Can I walk a little bit longer? Can I travel in more comfort? These are some of the really common ones that we get. And how much is it going to cost? I think Nick's slide said it really well. I think was it one euro 36 or something? And actually, some of the most cost effective evidence based interventions to improve longevity are nutritional interventions. Things like fiber, vitamin D, calcium, protein. All of these things have a really high level of evidence compared to some other newer, more novel technologies, and they're really cost-effective. Vitamin D, I think, costs about two cents per 10 microgram serving. I worked out from our from our own label. Most of our customers are not asking or saying, "What's my NAD level? How long are my telomeres? Are my siruin scavenging free radicals, or how active are my parts? I have never once heard any of those things from our customers. It's not to say they don't matter. The evidence gap. So when I'm talking to ingredient ingredient suppliers all the time, and I'm very immersed in clinical research, and a lot of the time, I'm seeing ingredients and the industry getting stuck in the first two blue sections of this. We're very focused on mechanism. We're very focused on biomarkers, but we're not focused on not just the clinical outcome, the customer outcome. What does the customer want? So, for example, if we take sleep, you know, I had a an ingredient the other day I was reading about, and they were constantly talking about the Pittsburgh Sleep Inventory, and I was like, a customer is not going to understand that. A customer wants to know, am I going to sleep better? Am I going to wake up feeling more refreshed? But it's our job as scientists and in the industry to help communicate these clinical benefits into something a consumer is going to understand, because consumers don't understand Eck depressive indexes, Pittsburgh, sleep relaxes, etc. What they do understand is how they're going to feel, and are they going to feel better taking that product? So I think I'll skip that slide actually because I think I covered it on the last one. So a little bit of a case study because it's a very hot topic in our business at the moment is NAD and NAD boosters. So, what do we know about NAD? I won't bore you with the research, but I think the most important thing I will take is a customer case study. Again, is we presented some concepts around cellular health and cellular aging to a group of customers about a month ago, and the feedback was absolutely fascinating because I'd never actually heard the customer, how the customers perceive NAD and cellular health. Not a single customer knew what NAD was. There was over 1000 people that we surveyed. Not a single one knew what NAD was. And when we surveyed, what do you think cellular health is as a concept? The answers were like playing Family Fortunes. It was quite quite incredible of the types of things people thought there was starting with fertility, immunity, recovery. There was there was a very low level of consumer understanding in this space. So when you start talking to customers about boosting NAD, most of our customers anyway don't even know what that is. And actually, from my perspective as a nutrition scientist, when I look at the research for nicotinamide riboside, nicotinamide mononucleotide, the outcome level data, if I think back to that last slide, is very very limited, especially when we compare it. I'm not sure if this is the right slide because there should be a nutrition. Okay, this is not the right slide, so I will. That's fine. Let me go back to this one. So the. yeah, the outcome-based data. One of the trials here is actually from a 2026 April this year metro analysis that looked at nicotinamide riboside, but it specifically looked at NAD boosting and outcomes. I think there's one trial that looks at improved walking speed in people over the age of 60 or something like that. But most people are not buying NAD for that. They're looking at it as the silver bullet or the elixir. But the research just isn't there. And like I said before, fiber, another big one, really hot topic at the moment. I'm sure if anybody's been to the US in the last six months, everything is protein plus fiber. For every seven grams of fiber we can give to a consumer, you're going to reduce your risk of coronary heart disease by about 9% and fiber is an extremely cheap intervention. And there's actually specific research in elderly people that if you give them fiber, it will reduce their risk of coronary heart disease. And actually, it's one of the biggest predictors of longevity from a nutritional intervention perspective. It might not be sexy, it might not be new, but it's very evidence-based. Skip on. I'm probably going to not do joint health, but yeah, okay. No, joint health is an interesting one as well because I think again we get lost in kind of muscle strength, boosting muscle mass and improving function. But what does the evidence say, and how do consumers understand this? So curcumin is our second best-selling ingredient globally. I think we sell one bottle a minute. I hope that statistic is still correct. But again, the research on curcumin is probably a good example of where we can communicate more than what we're allowed to communicate. So the on-hole claim for curcumin, I believe, is joint flexibility and joint comfort. But actually, there is some really strong evidence for curcumin and looking at knee osteoarthritis, improvement in movement, improvement in function, and reductions in systemic inflammation. And I'm going to finish with. Does anybody know who this man is? Nobody. Good. This man is called Kenton Brown. He is 81 years old, and he's just broken his own world record in the 100-meter sprint. He ran 100 meters in 14.4 seconds at the age of 81, and for any track and field people, that's a very quick time at the age of 81. But what I found more fascinating is he broke his own world record from the year before when he was 80. So again, a really inspires a fantastic, fantastic person to listen to an interview. He's a fantastic personality, but again, just more evidence that aging is not set. We can influence it. I think we can influence 80% of the way we age, and Kenton is a fantastic example of that. Thank you.

summary.Summary: Alex Glover, who leads Holland & Barrett's global own-label product formulation team, argued that consumers buy outcomes they can feel, not mechanisms [00:25]. He used a tortoise to show that ageing badly is not biologically fixed, and said the category should be about living better, not longer. H&B's data on millions of customers shows repeat purchase goes to products with a clearly communicated benefit (joint function, joint comfort, brain function), and its customer panels talk about playing with grandchildren and getting out of a chair, not sirtuins or telomeres. His evidence against mechanism-led novelty: of over 1000 customers surveyed, not one knew what NAD was, and the outcome-level data for nicotinamide riboside and mononucleotide is "very very limited", while cheap interventions (fibre, vitamin D, calcium, protein) have strong evidence; he gave about 9% lower coronary heart disease risk per seven grams of fibre and vitamin D at about two cents per 10 microgram serving. Curcumin, H&B's second best-selling ingredient globally ("one bottle a minute"), was his example of evidence stronger than the permitted claim.
summary.Key takeaways:
- Customers do not buy the mechanism; they buy how they feel and keep feeling, so the retailer's recurring questions are when will I feel it, what will I feel, can I measure it, and how much does it cost [00:25].
- H&B's biggest own-label sellers have a clearly communicated benefit (joint function, joint comfort, brain function); products that recite clinical literature do not sell as well [00:25].
- Ingredient suppliers get "stuck" in mechanism and biomarkers; the customer outcome is the gap (sleep example: the Pittsburgh Sleep Inventory means nothing to a shopper) [00:25].
- NAD: over 1000 customers surveyed and "not a single one knew what NAD was"; outcome-level data for NR and NMN is "very very limited" (he cited an April 2026 meta-analysis and one trial on walking speed in the over-60s) [00:25].

Alex Glover discusses the necessity of translating complex scientific mechanisms into tangible consumer outcomes to drive product sales and customer retention.

## Consumer Insights
**Translating Science**
**Alex** emphasizes that while researchers focus on biological mechanisms like sirtuins, telomeres, or **NAD**, consumers prioritize functional benefits. Customers do not use clinical language; they want to know if a product will help them play with grandchildren, walk without pain, or sleep more refreshingly. **Alex** notes that the highest sales in the **Holland & Barrett** own-label portfolio come from products with clearly communicated benefits for joint function, brain function, and comfort.

**Market Realities**
**Alex** highlights a significant gap in consumer understanding regarding longevity science. In a survey of over 1,000 people, not a single respondent knew what **NAD** was. While there is high interest in "cellular health," consumer definitions are vague, covering everything from fertility to immunity. This suggests that marketing novel ingredients requires bridging the gap between clinical biomarkers and everyday feelings.

## Product Strategy
**Evidence Based Interventions**
**Alex** argues that cost-effective, traditional nutritional interventions often have stronger evidence bases than newer technologies. Examples include:
* **Fiber**: Reduces coronary heart disease risk by approximately 9% per seven grams of intake.
* **Vitamin D**: Highly cost-effective, costing roughly two cents per 10 microgram serving.
* **Curcumin**: A top-selling ingredient globally (one bottle sold per minute) that supports joint flexibility and reduces systemic inflammation.

**The Longevity Gap**
The discussion contrasts the "longevity" category—which implies living longer—with the goal of helping people "live better." **Alex** points out that many industry players get stuck in the "blue sections" of research, focusing on mechanisms and biomarkers rather than clinical outcomes. The primary questions from retailers and customers remain: "When am I going to feel a benefit?" and "How much is it going to cost?"

**Two Waves** is a digital platform designed to streamline the manufacturing ecosystem between brands, manufacturers, and ingredient suppliers.

## Market Challenges
The manufacturing market is projected by **Grandview Research** to grow at over 12 percent annually, exceeding $60 billion by 2030. However, current processes suffer from significant inefficiencies:
* Lack of visibility in specific product categories.
* Incomplete inquiries and fragmented communication across multiple email threads.
* High operational costs due to wasted time organizing data and searching for agreements.
* Lost opportunities resulting from missed offers or inquiries that do not reach the right partners.

## Platform Solutions
**Viktor** and **Matthew** introduced **Two Waves** as a tool to centralize quoting and negotiation through several key modules:
* **New Partnerships**: Instead of one-to-one outreach, one inquiry automatically reaches all verified manufacturers within a specific category, allowing for rapid comparison of structured offers.
* **Standardized Quoting**: The platform uses structured templates tailored to product categories to eliminate "communication noise" and ensure all key information is present.
* **Negotiation Management**: Users can manage quoting variants and track the full history of negotiations in a single location. 
* **Feedback Loops**: If an inquiry or offer is declined, the system provides a specific reason to improve future interactions.

## Security Infrastructure
**Matthew** addressed the risks associated with traditional communication methods like phone calls and emails, where data control is easily lost once information enters an inbox. To mitigate these risks, **Two Waves** implements:
* Mandatory company verification for all users to ensure participants are interacting only with verified entities.
* Enhanced control over how sensitive information is shared during the initial stages of business relationships.

The panel discussed the evolving landscape of the nutraceutical industry, focusing on scientific evidence, regulatory challenges, and technological integration.

## Industry Trends
**Alexandra**, **Matt**, and **Alex** highlighted the increasing demand for evidence-based products and high-quality communication.
*   **Alexandra** emphasized that consumers are increasingly well-informed but often rely on unqualified sources, necessitating better communication of factual ingredient claims.
*   **Matt** suggested a revolution in clinical trials, advocating for high-dose studies on individuals with actual health problems rather than healthy subjects to generate more meaningful data.
*   **Alex** noted that consumers prioritize solving specific problems and prefer clear, specialized messaging over brands that attempt to market too many ingredients or claims simultaneously.

## Regulatory Challenges
**Joanna** and **Martina** addressed the friction between innovation and legal frameworks.
*   **Joanna** explained that current food laws were designed for common ingredients like vitamin C and D, making it difficult for innovators to use clinical trial data to support new claims. She urged R&D teams to involve lawyers early in the development process to ensure compliance is a "shield" rather than a "heartbreak."
*   **Martina** observed that legislation often acts as an obstacle for CDMOs and advised businesses not to simply chase every market gap but to focus on deep understanding and consumer needs.
*   **Matt** raised concerns regarding the speed of European regulations compared to the **U.S.**, noting that a three-year delay in approval can make the net present value of new ingredients economically unviable.

## Supply and Technology
The discussion concluded with the impact of supply chain volatility and artificial intelligence.
*   **Matt** warned of a looming collapse in the fish oil supply chain due to aquaculture industry competition and potential traceability issues involving illegal fishing. 
*   **Alex** noted that retailers must proactively manage lead times and prepare for price increases or shifts in consumer preference if core ingredients like omega-3 become unavailable.
*   **Joanna** and **Alexandra** discussed the role of **AI**, noting its utility in searching peer-reviewed databases and managing factory sensors. **Joanna** stressed the importance of keeping a "human in the loop" to maintain legal integrity and trust, while **Matt** predicted that proficiency in operating **AI** tools will become a mandatory job requirement within two years.

Marit Weinstra from **HMT** discusses the evolution of the probiotic market and shifting consumer expectations toward holistic gut health.

## Market Evolution
The probiotic category has moved through several distinct eras, transitioning from basic awareness to complex ecosystem management.
*   **First Era**: Focused on the concept of "good" vs "bad" bacteria, popularized by **Yakult** as a daily ritual.
*   **Second Era**: Led by **Danone Activia**, which focused on making intangible benefits like digestion more tangible via branding.
*   **Third Era**: Centered on technology and survival, where the primary promise was ensuring bacteria arrive alive in the gut.
*   **Current Era**: Shifting from simply adding bacteria to nourishing the entire gut ecosystem, focusing on terms like the gut barrier and fermentation.

## Strategic Shifts
To succeed in the current "jungle" of products, brands must follow four new industry rules to build consumer trust and clarity.
*   **Quality over Quantity**: Moving away from competing solely on high CFU counts (e.g., 50 billion or 100 billion) toward proven, niche expertise such as metabolic health.
*   **Ecosystem Nourishment**: Transitioning from adding single strains to providing plant diversity and fibers that proactively feed existing gut flora.
*   **Measurable Benefits**: Shifting from invisible promises to felt or measured results, utilizing microbiome tests or apps for early adopters while ensuring mass-market consumers feel immediate physical differences.
*   **Consumer-Centric Formats**: Moving from functional supplements toward desirable everyday food formats, similar to how **Poppi** approaches the category.

## Branding Strategy
Because many health claims are restricted in Europe compared to the U.S., brands must rely on emotional value rather than just rational science. 
*   Building a "double IP" involves combining rational scientific evidence with an emotional brand identity to ensure long-term protection and market presence. 
*   Success requires turning scientific innovation into a consumer-centric value proposition that provides clarity amidst excessive market options.

**Sacco** is an agile, family-owned company with global operations including manufacturing plants in Italy (Como and Milan) and the US (Wisconsin). Their infrastructure supports various production needs:
*   **CSL** (Milan): Specialized in pharmaceutical API probiotics.
*   **Sacosystem Australia** (Brisbane): A pilot facility focused on next-generation bacteria, exotic strains, and LVPs.

**Symbio** is a synergistic mixture of *L. paracasi* and *L. rhamnosus* isolated from the Italian Marche region.
*   **Clinical Findings**: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled study of 97 subjects over six months, **Symbio** increased gut microbiota diversity (Akkermansia, Bifidobacteria) and short-chain fatty acids like butyrate.

*   **Longevity**: Blood analysis indicated a decrease in the rate of telomere shortening, a key marker of biological aging.

Otter.ai's automatic summary, as received. Not ours.

The meeting focused on innovative probiotic dosage forms and clinically tested probiotic strain technologies.

## Dosage Form Innovation
**Miguel** from **SPI Pharma** presented advanced delivery systems designed to improve consumer experience and stability.
*   **Composol Pro Tab**: A polyol-based, low water activity platform used to create chewable probiotic tablets with low compression forces to ensure probiotic survival.
*   **Effer Soda**: A partially transformed sodium bicarbonate product that creates a protective layer, enhancing stability in effervescent tablets, stick packs, or sachets. This technology can also produce a "delicate fizz" in fast-melting solutions to mask bitterness.
*   **Orally Disintegrating Tablets (ODT)**: Fast-melting platforms designed for populations with dysphagia, such as children and the elderly, allowing for consumption without water.

## Probiotic Research
**Mihail Jakubowski** of **Nordic Biotic** detailed scientific advancements in specialized probiotic strains and their metabolic functions.
*   **Northbiotic Mental Balance**: Developed with the **Polish Academy of Sciences**, this blend uses **Lactobacillus plantarum 140** (producing GABA) and **Bifidobacterium breve 010** (producing vitamin B free). An eight-week study of 227 students demonstrated statistical efficacy in improving sleep quality and managing stress.
*   **Microplastic Management**: A novel approach using two specific strains for gut cleansing:
    1.  **Lactobacillus acidophilus 120**: Aggregates and binds microplastic particles.
    2.  **Lactobacillus fermentum 160**: Pushes microplastics away from the mucosal lining to facilitate removal.
*   Human studies regarding the microplastic-binding technology are currently in progress.

## Strategic Partnerships
Both speakers emphasized opportunities for collaborative development between manufacturers and researchers. 
*   **Miguel** invited participants to use **SPI Pharma's** concept-driven approach to expand existing portfolios into new dosage forms like hydration sticks or chewable probiotics. 
*   **Mihail Jakubowski** proposed the **Plastic Gut-Free Initiative**, inviting brand owners and CDMOs to participate in co-development projects centered on microbiome research and genomics.

Action items: none returned.
